comment: Class is difficult if you have no coding experience, but Mattson really wants to help see you succeed. Go to office hours!

He is always willing to help and his tests are fairly simple if you try and understand the subject. you dont even need to have coding experience or need to know how to write code out of scratch, you just need to understand the logic behind the code and the concepts. he always explains each concept well.

This class is hard if you have no coding experience, but Mattson is always available if you need help. Exams require a lot of prep, but you do get a cheat sheet to help. There are only a few grades in the course, but there is plenty of extra credit to help boost your grade. Overall would highly recommend.

Best professor I ever had. Mattson set me down the path of technology with his Python introduction to machine learning. 3 years later I am now a software engineer out of school and it wouldn't have been without his excellent teaching inspiring me to get into technology!

This is for INFO 301. he cares and is enthusiastic. just put in the effort needed and you will love the class overtime. At first it will be difficult if you don't have prior experience but trust me it will be better.
Mattson should be the role model teacher in RSB. The GOAT

This review is about INFO 302 not 303 (didn't give me the option to choose 302). 

Mattson is great but he is new to teaching this course and it shows. Not a lot of teaching, just a lot of lecturing and talking at you. You copy his code. He makes exams pretty hard, but then sometimes will give extra credit when the class doesn't do well.

Very chill guy. Your grade is made up of 3 tests and 1 final project that are equally weighted. No midterm or final. Never had HW either. You basically watch 1-3 hours of material by yourself and go over them in class. Not sure if the class was like that due to the virus or not though

Dr. Mattson was awesome for Machine Learning. The course was pretty new, but he presented it very well. One exam and two case projects, which weren't too difficult but took a bit of time. He used a flipped classroom model, where the class time was spent reinforcing ideas and doing exercises. Really nice person, awesome content, 10/10.

Easy class and but he has long videos to explain the topics that can get tiring at times. But he makes sure you learn the content well. He has great knowledge about what he teaches and makes the topics look not as complicated. Definitely recommend him if you want to learn excel, access and Tableau.

Dr. Mattson is the most helpful professor I've had. The course is designed to be almost too hard, which can be annoying, but he grades accordingly. He is extremely helpful outside of class, and even in class during exams when you are stuck. That being said, you still will have to put in a lot of work to get an A.

Fine I guess, but very frustrating. Basically dont learn in class, just given scenarios to work on and videos with "answers" to practice outside class. Had to teach myself everything but helpful outside class for questions. Test and project grades ONLY. Group project is a sht show if you have a bad group -randomly assigned. No good options really.

Mattson cares about his students success more than any professor I've had at UR. Had him for MGMT 325 and 375 and he couldn't have been more helpful. Always willing to meet with students outside of class and is super helpful when he does. Attendance is optional, but if you fall behind in 375 it's almost impossible to catch up.
The best person I have ever seen in the business school. My life mentor and savior. Cannot thank you more!
